notes.key_messages: Candidates are advised to: • give a single response, either single word or short phrase, f or each gap in Question 1 • respond to all parts of Question 2 in the tense indicated • use simple linking words in Question 2, f or example when giving opinions/explanations • choose the option in Question 3 which allows them to show what they know • give brief additional details in response to individual tasks in Question 3 • plan and organise answers into a coherent piece of writing, using extended sentences where possible.
notes.general_comments: Overall, candidates found the paper accessible, but common errors resulted in some candidates not able to reach higher marks. Candidates should be careful about the influence of words in their own language. Meaning was f requently compromised when the f ollowing were replaced by a non-French word: agréable, autre, pays, pollution, quand. To convey their ideas, candidates must use a correct subject/verb accord in an appropriate tense. It is important to copy correctly vocabulary given in the rubrics. The misspelling or incorrect gender of améliorer, difficultés, personne, problèmes environnementaux, quartier sometimes compromised communication. Candidates are regularly asked to comment on advantages or disadvantages, and they should be able to recognise such tasks and adapt the rubric used, e.g. l’avantage est / les avantages sont / l’inconvénient est / les inconvénients sont. Some candidates used trop/plus instead of très. These are not synonyms and can convey a dif f erent and sometimes ambiguous meaning Candidates should be able to write correct sentences and link them where possible using structures listed in the syllabus, e.g. conjunctions (où, qui, que, quand, lorsque, si), verbal phrases (après avoir/être, avant de, depuis, pour, afin de), correct prepositional linkage of verbs. Object pronouns, strong negatives and uses of the comparative would also enhance the narrative.
notes.3a: Une personne âgée dans ma famille For Task 1, candidates were able to give details about their elderly relative, e.g. je suis allé chez ma grand- mère qui a 80 ans / mon grand père habite au Brésil. A f ew candidates did not know âgée and some described a f riend. Candidates gave a range of different information to describe their visit in Task 2, e.g. j’ai pris l’avion pour aller voir mon grand-père / nous avons fait une promenade / j’ai aidé ma grand-mère à faire les courses. Candidates who understood Task 3 offered a range of information about how this person spends their time, e.g. il rencontre ses amis au café / elle joue aux cartes / il regarde la télévision. Candidates answered Task 4 with a range of difficulties faced by old people, e.g. les personnes âgées ont des problems de santé / elles sont seules à la maison / ils ont des difficultés avec la technologie. Task 5 was straightforward f or candidates who could use a conditional tense correctly, e.g. je voudrais organiser une fête pour son anniversaire / je voudrais aller la voir avec toute la famille.
notes.3b: La vie dans mon quartier In answer to Task 1, candidates established the context of their visit with a simple statement, e.g. j’ai fait partie d’une association qui plante des arbres dans mon quartier / j’ai participé à un tournoi de foot. For Task 2, reactions to the experience ranged from the simple idea, e.g. j’ai adore cette activité, to the more compex, e.g. c’était une activité enrichissante / je pense que protéger notre planète est important. Some candidates only achieved partial completion of the task as they could not produce an appropriate past tense. For Task 3, candidates proposed a range of ideas, e.g. mon quartier est très tranquille / il n’y a pas de crime dans le quartier / les gens sont sympas. Some expanded their answer by mentioning disadvantages, e.g. il n’y a pas assez de poubelles, in anticipation of the f ollowing task. For Task 4, candidates also proposed a range of ideas, e.g. il y a trop de voitures / les gens jettent les déchets dans la rue / l’air est pollué à cause de la circulation et des embouteillages. Task 5 was straightforward for candidates who could use a conditional tense correctly, e.g. j’aimerais utiliser les transports en commun plus souvent / je voudrais acheter une voiture électrique / je voudrais planter des arbres et recycler le plastique.
